content: Advance M0130/W0132 with a host-independent memory visibility model for the staging baseline. Define generation-bound host/device access ownership, non-coherent flush and invalidate range alignment, timeline admission, and teardown rejection without claiming physical VkDeviceMemory or external-handle qualification.

Visibility operations are explicit observations over one allocation: host writes require a host-to-device flush before device reads, device writes require a device-to-host invalidate before host reads, coherent allocations accept no-op visibility operations, and every range is rounded to the atom-size within the allocation. Stale generation, zero/out-of-range/overflow ranges, and visibility while the allocation is in flight are rejected.

Content revision 96d3a55 adds MemoryVisibilityLedger with generation-bound allocation registration, host/device dirty-range tracking, non-coherent atom-size range normalization, explicit flush/invalidate, submission completion, and in-flight unregister/configure rejection. MemoryStatus remains the existing staging/timeline status surface; visibility uses a separate status enum and string mapping.

Memory visibility positive and negative fixtures pass for coherent and non-coherent allocations, partial dirty-range flushing, device-write invalidation, stale generations, range bounds, duplicate registration, timeline ordering, in-flight teardown, and reconfiguration. Full Vulkan CTest passed 88/88.
